title: Core init workflow split across hidden reference breaks Phase 2 continuation
description:
## Discovered in
Manual Phase 2 continuation review on 2026-04-18 after a successful Phase 1 install/restart flow.

## Problem
The resource-backed `/opencode-coder/init` command tells the model to "Initialize and set up opencode-coder for this project", but the actual setup workflow is split across `coder-core` references in a way that makes the continuation path easy to miss.

Observed behavior:
- The command loads `coder-core`.
- The model naturally reads `references/installation-setup.md` and `references/mode-runtime.md`.
- It does **not** naturally read `references/init-dispatch.md`.
- As a result, Phase 2 continuation after restart can stall even when the project is installed correctly.

Why this happens:
- `init-dispatch.md` is really part of installation/setup, not a distinct concept.
- `coder-core/SKILL.md` currently lists both `installation-setup.md` and `init-dispatch.md` under the same top-level workflow, which hides the real instruction path instead of making it obvious.
- The command file is too thin to force the model toward the missing reference.

## Expected
The core installation/setup reference should directly include the setup-continuation workflow so that when the command says "Initialize and set up opencode-coder for this project", the model naturally reads the right reference and continues setup.

## Actual
The continuation/setup logic is isolated in `ai-resources/skills/coder-core/references/init-dispatch.md`, which the model can skip.

## Fix direction
- Merge the useful workflow content from `references/init-dispatch.md` into `references/installation-setup.md`.
- Remove the separate `init-dispatch.md` concept.
- Update `coder-core/SKILL.md` so the top-level setup workflow points to the right core setup references without the hidden extra file.
- Update any tests that currently protect the split-file structure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `installation-setup.md` includes the setup-continuation workflow currently isolated in `init-dispatch.md`
- [ ] `init-dispatch.md` is removed
- [ ] `coder-core/SKILL.md` no longer references a separate init-dispatch file
- [ ] `/opencode-coder/init` command wording remains simple while naturally leading the model to the right setup reference
- [ ] Related tests are updated

## Files to Modify
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/SKILL.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/references/installation-setup.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/references/init-dispatch.md
- tests/unit/docs-lifecycle-contract.test.ts
close_reason: Merged continuation workflow into installation-setup.md, removed init-dispatch.md, and updated tests.

title: Phase 2 init does not resume cleanly after successful Phase 1 restart
description:
## Discovered in
User manual validation of `opencode-coder-bsr` on 2026-04-18.

## Expected
After Phase 1 succeeds in an empty project, closing and reopening OpenCode should allow the user to run `/opencode-coder/init` again and continue into the resource-backed init flow cleanly.

## Actual
Phase 1 worked, but after closing OpenCode and restarting it, the user could not really continue with Phase 2.

## Repro
1. Start OpenCode in an empty project.
2. Run `/opencode-coder/init` and complete Phase 1 successfully.
3. Close OpenCode.
4. Reopen OpenCode in the same project.
5. Try to continue with `/opencode-coder/init`.
6. Observe that Phase 2 does not resume cleanly.

## Impact
This blocks the intended two-step init flow even when Phase 1 succeeds. The standard setup experience is incomplete until restart/continuation works reliably.

## Notes needed
Need follow-up triage to capture the exact post-restart behavior:
- was `/opencode-coder/init` missing?
- did Phase 1 bootstrap show again instead of the resource-backed command?
- did command execution fail?
- were installed surfaces missing or not detected?

## Related Work
- Acceptance review for `opencode-coder-bsr`
- broader two-step init work under `opencode-coder-bwrr`
close_reason: Closed as resolved by fixing the hidden core continuation reference split under opencode-coder-xp0.

title: Adopt coder-support as standard generic support bundle
description:
## Description
Adopt `package/coder-support` as the standard generic support bundle in the normal opencode-coder setup flow. The standard plugin/package/docs path should prefer `package/coder-support` for generic development/design/architecture tooling, while `package/code-simplify` and `skill/complexity-review` remain available as legacy or standalone surfaces and are not removed.

This change should simplify the setup flow by removing the non-`coder-*` special case for `package/complexity-review`. The `src/` impact should stay focused on optional package discovery and bootstrap guidance; runtime phase detection and other core plugin behavior should remain intact unless a real break is found.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Standard optional package discovery/setup uses `package/coder-support`
- [ ] The `src/` setup flow no longer needs a special `package/complexity-review` branch
- [ ] Package surfaces, docs, and examples use `package/coder-support` for the normal generic-support flow
- [ ] Legacy/standalone `code-simplify` and `complexity-review` surfaces remain available where intentionally needed
- [ ] Impacted tests/harnesses are updated for the new standard package set
- [ ] Full Phase 1 manual validation is performed in an empty project: start OpenCode, run `/opencode-coder/init`, confirm package installation flow works, and confirm the selected mode is persisted correctly
- [ ] Full automated validation is performed, including `bun test` and the e2e coverage, with any unrelated failures tracked explicitly
close_reason: Coder-support adoption implemented, tested, and accepted; unrelated follow-up issues remain tracked separately.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Dependency graph is inverted. What: .4 (acceptance review) blocks .3 (tests), which blocks .1 (src) and .2 (docs). The correct order is .1/.2 (implementation) → .3 (tests) → .4 (acceptance review). Currently no task can start because the acceptance review task blocks everything. Why: execution will be impossible — the ready queue is empty since every task is blocked by its successor. Suggested action: reverse dependencies so .1 and .2 have no blockers (or depend on each other if order matters), .3 depends on .1 and .2, and .4 depends on .3.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter

Also clarified .1 must update both complexity-review references in init-install-guide.ts, clarified .2 must remove the phantom package/complexity-review line from ai.package.yaml while keeping skill/complexity-review, and removed focused test/manual ownership overlap from .3.

title: Init command and skill routing still expose dispatcher internals
description:
## Discovered in
User review on 2026-04-18 after the naming cleanup in `opencode-coder-pa1`.

## Problem
The current resource-backed init wording is still shaped around implementation details instead of user-facing workflows.

Specific problems called out in review:
1. `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md` became worse after the cleanup. The command now talks about being an installed-skill dispatcher instead of simply describing the init workflow.
2. `ai-resources/skills/coder-core/SKILL.md` now exposes two setup-looking workflows:
   - `Init/setup guidance`
   - `Installed-skill init dispatch`
   From a user-facing skill surface this looks like two different setup workflows even though it is really one init/setup capability with plugin/runtime details underneath.
3. `ai-resources/skills/coder-beads/SKILL.md` and similar skill surfaces use caller-oriented workflow names like `Run beads init workflow when dispatched by coder-core`. That is awkward and wrong at the skill surface level. Workflow names should describe the skill's own capability (for example beads setup/init), not the caller/call-path.
4. The fix for this issue should stay scoped to the resource-backed command/skill/reference surfaces and related tests. Do not widen it into `README.md` or `docs/user-guide/getting-started.md`.

## Expected
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md` should use simple init/setup wording again instead of dispatcher-heavy wording.
- `coder-core` should present one coherent init/setup workflow surface rather than two setup-sounding entries.
- `coder-beads` / `coder-docs` workflow routing should use capability-oriented names such as beads setup/init or docs setup/init, not caller-oriented phrasing.
- Detailed implementation/dispatch mechanics may exist in references where needed, but the top-level command/skill surfaces should stay simple and user-facing.

## Actual
- The current command/skill cleanup removed some phase naming but still leaves the user-facing surfaces shaped around plugin dispatch mechanics.
- Core now appears to have two setup workflows.
- Beads/docs workflow names are phrased from the dispatcher's perspective instead of the skill's perspective.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md` is simplified to user-facing init/setup wording
- [ ] `coder-core/SKILL.md` no longer presents two competing setup-sounding workflows
- [ ] `coder-beads/SKILL.md` and `coder-docs/SKILL.md` use capability-oriented workflow names
- [ ] Detailed dispatch mechanics, if still needed, stay in references rather than top-level routing text
- [ ] Related tests are updated to protect the simplified skill/command architecture
- [ ] `README.md` and `docs/user-guide/getting-started.md` are not modified as part of this specific cleanup

## Files to Modify
- ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/SKILL.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-beads/SKILL.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/SKILL.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/references/
- ai-resources/skills/coder-beads/references/
- ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/
- tests/unit/beads-service.test.ts
- tests/unit/docs-lifecycle-contract.test.ts

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Clarified by review: the coder-core init reference must not talk about /opencode-coder/init or point to other skills' reference files. It should describe project initialization in skill-local, capability-oriented terms: load installed skills (especially installed skills whose names start with coder-), determine which skills define initialization/setup workflows, determine a logical initialization order, and run the project setup/initialization work for each relevant skill. Avoid dispatcher/caller-oriented wording in top-level command/skill/reference surfaces.

title: Phase 2 init docs should be Phase-2-only and move detailed workflow out of SKILL.md
description:
## Discovered in
User review of the current uncommitted install/setup implementation on 2026-04-18.

## Problem
The current Phase 2 work documents behavior in the wrong surfaces:

1. `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md` currently tells the agent to detect Phase 1 vs Phase 2 and run a two-pass workflow, but in reality Phase 1 is handled by the plugin runtime bootstrap override (`config-hook.ts` injects the bootstrap template and suppresses the resource-backed command in Phase 1).
2. `ai-resources/skills/coder-core/SKILL.md`, `ai-resources/skills/coder-beads/SKILL.md`, and `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/SKILL.md` currently embed detailed init contracts / step-by-step workflow text directly in SKILL.md. That is not the intended skill style for this repo; SKILL.md should stay as concise routing/ownership surface and the detailed workflow should live in proper referenced docs/commands.

## Expected
- `/opencode-coder/init` command markdown should describe only the Phase 2 resource-backed behavior it actually owns.
- Phase 1 handling should remain plugin-owned and not be redundantly described as command logic in the resource-backed command file.
- SKILL.md files should remain concise. Detailed init workflows should move to appropriate reference docs / workflow surfaces instead of being embedded inline in multiple SKILL.md files.

## Actual
- The command file describes two-pass phase detection that does not actually run there in Phase 1.
- Multiple SKILL.md files now contain detailed init-procedure contracts that should not live directly in SKILL.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md` is rewritten to cover only Phase 2 resource-backed init behavior
- [ ] `coder-core` keeps concise routing in SKILL.md and points to a proper reference/workflow surface for detailed Phase 2 behavior
- [ ] `coder-beads` and `coder-docs` remove inline step-by-step init contracts from SKILL.md and route to proper reference/workflow surfaces instead
- [ ] Any tests introduced for the prior inline-contract wording are updated to assert the corrected architecture instead
- [ ] The resulting wording matches actual runtime behavior (`config-hook.ts` Phase 1 override vs Phase 2 resource-backed command)

## Files to Modify
- ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/SKILL.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-beads/SKILL.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/SKILL.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/references/
- ai-resources/skills/coder-beads/references/
- ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/
- tests/unit/beads-service.test.ts
- tests/unit/docs-lifecycle-contract.test.ts
close_reason: Updated Phase 2 init docs architecture: command is Phase-2-only, SKILL routing is concise, detailed init contracts moved to references, and related tests now assert reference-driven boundaries.

title: Existing epic/task IDs stop resolving after follow-up issue creation
description:
## Discovered in
Acceptance/verification work for `opencode-coder-bwrr` on 2026-04-18 while filing follow-up issues after manual review.

## Expected
Existing epic and child task IDs should remain resolvable in the same local beads database after acceptance review and follow-up bug creation. Commands such as `bd show <epic-id>`, `bd show <task-id>`, `bd list`, and `bd status` should continue to show the previously active work.

## Actual
After follow-up issue creation, previously used hierarchical IDs such as `opencode-coder-bwrr` and `opencode-coder-bwrr.4` stopped resolving locally. `bd status` / `bd list` showed only newly created standalone bugs instead of the earlier epic/task set.

## Repro
Session-derived repro so far:
1. Work in the repo using an existing epic with hierarchical child IDs.
2. Close child tasks and run acceptance verification that creates follow-up bugs.
3. Afterwards run `bd show <epic-id>`, `bd show <task-id>`, `bd list`, and `bd status`.
4. Observe that the original epic/task IDs no longer resolve and the visible issue set collapses to the newly created standalone bugs.

## Impact
Tracker state becomes unreliable mid-session. Acceptance work can no longer reference the original epic/tasks, and follow-up issues cannot be linked confidently to the work that discovered them.

## Evidence
- 2026-04-18 repo session in `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder`
- `bd show opencode-coder-bwrr` -> not found
- `bd show opencode-coder-bwrr.4` -> not found
- `bd status` / `bd list` only showed the new standalone bugs

## Notes
This is not yet reduced to a minimal standalone repro. It may be a beads database/state-management bug or a verifier-session side effect, but the observed symptom is real and it disrupted tracker-based execution in this repo.
close_reason: Closing as session-specific tracker artifact without standalone repro; reviewer judged it weak/not actionable as a product bug.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Review verdict: LIKELY NOT A PRODUCT BUG — session/tooling artifact. What: the 'lost IDs' symptom almost certainly means the beads database file (.beads/issues.jsonl) was modified during the session (it shows as staged-modified in git status). Epic/task IDs from a previous session or branch may have been overwritten when follow-up bugs were created, or the epic was created in a different beads database state that got replaced. Why it matters: filing this as a P1 beads-database bug without a minimal standalone repro risks chasing a phantom. The repro steps are session-specific and unreproducible. Suggested action: downgrade to P3 or close. If you want to keep it, reframe as 'investigate whether beads issue creation can corrupt or overwrite existing issues in issues.jsonl' — but only if someone can reproduce it outside this specific session.

title: Documented public ai.repo.yaml manifest URL returns 404
description:
## Discovered in
Acceptance review of `opencode-coder-bwrr` / `opencode-coder-bwrr.4` on 2026-04-18.

## Expected
The documented public Phase 1 bootstrap path should fetch a real published manifest and allow `aimgr repo apply-manifest <url>` to proceed in a fresh environment.

## Actual
The documented URL `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder/main/ai-resources/ai.repo.yaml` returned HTTP 404 during manual acceptance, so the public bootstrap path could not complete end-to-end.

## Repro
1. Create an isolated fresh-project environment with `bun run test:manual -- --mode=shell --fixture=empty-project`.
2. Follow the documented Phase 1 public bootstrap path from `/opencode-coder/init`, `README.md`, or `docs/user-guide/getting-started.md`.
3. Fetch the raw GitHub URL directly or run `aimgr repo apply-manifest <url>`.
4. Observe the 404 response.

## Impact
Acceptance of the install/setup epic is blocked because the documented public bootstrap path is not actually reachable yet. Fresh users following the published guidance would fail before Phase 1 can complete.

## Likely Fix Direction
Either publish `ai-resources/ai.repo.yaml` at the documented public path or update the code/docs/template to the real published manifest location before closing acceptance.

## Evidence
- Acceptance review session on 2026-04-18
- Manual launcher artifacts under `.manual-test-runs/`
- Local working tree already contains `ai-resources/ai.repo.yaml`, so this may resolve when the change is landed/published.
close_reason: Not a product defect: 404 is due to current ai.repo.yaml change not being pushed/published yet; resolves when current install/setup work is landed.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Review verdict: NOT A PRODUCT BUG — this is a session artifact. What: ai-resources/ai.repo.yaml exists locally as an untracked file (git status shows '??'). The 404 occurs because the install/setup work hasn't been committed and pushed yet. Once the pending changes land on main, this URL will resolve. Why it matters: tracking this as a P1 bug implies a product defect when none exists — it's just unpushed work. Suggested action: close as not-a-bug. The fix is simply landing the already-implemented install/setup changes. No separate fix needed.

title: Simplify src package discovery and bootstrap guidance
description:
## Description
Update the `src/` setup flow so the normal generic support package is `package/coder-support`. This should remove the explicit `package/complexity-review` corner case and let the `package/coder*` pattern drive optional package discovery more generally.

## Instructions
1. Update `src/service/aimgr-service.ts` optional package discovery so it relies on the `package/coder*` pattern and no longer manually adds `package/complexity-review` as a special case.
2. Inspect related `src/` code to confirm whether anything else breaks because of this package change; keep the runtime impact limited to real affected surfaces.
3. Update `src/templates/init-install-guide.ts` so optional package discovery/examples reference `package/coder-support` and remove the non-pattern special-case wording. This includes both current `complexity-review` references in the file (the explicit add-on note and the example package-name list).
4. Update the focused tests for this behavior (`tests/unit/service/aimgr-service.test.ts` and `tests/integration/plugin.test.ts` if needed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/service/aimgr-service.ts` no longer special-cases `package/complexity-review`
- [ ] `src/templates/init-install-guide.ts` describes optional package discovery via the general `package/coder*` pattern and no longer includes the old `complexity-review` special-case examples
- [ ] No additional `src/` breakage is left unexplained
- [ ] Focused impacted tests pass

## Files to Modify
- src/service/aimgr-service.ts
- src/templates/init-install-guide.ts
- tests/unit/service/aimgr-service.test.ts
- tests/integration/plugin.test.ts
close_reason: Removed complexity-review special-casing, switched optional discovery/docs guidance to package/coder* including coder-support, and verified with focused unit+integration tests.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: aimgr-service.ts special case is correctly identified. What: lines 188-199 explicitly add package/complexity-review outside the coder* pattern. The plan correctly identifies this as the special case to remove. The coder-support package already matches the coder* pattern (name is 'coder-support'), so once the special case is removed, coder-support will be auto-discovered. No issues with this task's src scope — it's accurate.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: init-install-guide.ts has two complexity-review references to update. What: line 90 mentions complexity-review as an explicitly supported add-on, and line 95 lists it as an example package name. title: bd create --deps rejects hierarchical issue IDs resolved by bd show
description:
## Discovered in
Acceptance verification follow-up filing on 2026-04-18 while creating bugs discovered during review of `opencode-coder-bwrr`.

## Expected
If `bd show <hierarchical-id>` resolves an issue successfully, that same hierarchical ID should also be accepted by `bd create --deps ...` when creating a dependency.

## Actual
`bd create --deps discovered-from:opencode-coder-bwrr.4 ...` warned that `opencode-coder-bwrr.4` was not found, even though `bd show opencode-coder-bwrr.4` resolved earlier in the same repository session.

## Repro
1. From `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder`, run `bd show opencode-coder-bwrr.4`.
2. Then run `bd create --type bug --deps discovered-from:opencode-coder-bwrr.4 --title "tmp" --description "tmp"`.
3. Observe the dependency warning.

## Impact
Follow-up bugs discovered during acceptance cannot be linked cleanly to hierarchical acceptance/task IDs, which weakens tracker history and makes later review harder.

## Evidence
- Verification session on 2026-04-18 while creating follow-up issue `opencode-coder-axu`.
close_reason: Closing as duplicate/session artifact tied to non-resolving hierarchical IDs in the same session; reviewer judged it not a separate product defect.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Review verdict: LIKELY DUPLICATE / CONSEQUENCE OF oo5. What: if the hierarchical IDs stopped resolving (oo5), then of course --deps referencing those IDs would also fail. This is the same root cause, not a separate bug. The description even says 'bd show resolved earlier in the same session' — meaning it worked before the state corruption from oo5 happened. Why it matters: tracking a symptom separately from its cause creates duplicate work and confusing tracker history. Suggested action: close as duplicate of oo5, or if oo5 is closed as session artifact, close this too.

title: Team-mode beads init can exceed default 120s timeout
description:
## Discovered in
Manual Phase 2 acceptance validation for `opencode-coder-bwrr` on 2026-04-18.

## Expected
Team-mode Phase 2 beads initialization should complete within the default agent bash timeout, or the flow should explicitly allow a longer-running init step.

## Actual
During Phase 2 team-mode validation, the inner `bd init --skip-agents` step exceeded the 120000ms timeout. A later `bd status` check indicated the beads workspace eventually became healthy, so the operation appears to finish eventually but too slowly for the default execution budget.

## Repro
1. Prepare an `empty-project` launcher workspace with local working-tree resources.
2. Set `.coder/opencode-coder.yaml` to `mode: team`.
3. Install `package/coder-core`, `package/coder-beads`, `package/coder-docs`, and `package/complexity-review` into `.opencode/`.
4. Run `opencode run --command opencode-coder/init --format json`.
5. Observe the `coder-beads` Phase 2 step run `bd init --skip-agents` and exceed the default timeout.

## Impact
Phase 2 team-mode setup can appear to fail under normal agent time budgets even when the underlying beads init eventually succeeds. This can block or confuse setup automation.

## Evidence
- Manual launcher artifact: `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder/.manual-test-runs/run-FHVtcp`
- Session output artifact: `/home/hans/.local/share/opencode/tool-output/tool_da11378ef001wxNuKJMxCbXXR2`

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Review verdict: VALID bug, well-scoped. What: bd init --skip-agents exceeding 120s in a team-mode launcher environment is a real problem that will hit any agent-driven setup automation. The description, repro, and evidence are solid. Why it matters: if Phase 2 team-mode init reliably times out under default agent budgets, automated setup is broken for team mode. P2 is appropriate. Suggested action: keep as-is. This should be fixed as a near-term follow-up — either bd init needs to be faster, or the init command needs to set an explicit longer timeout for this step. Defer from the current install/setup commit but prioritize it next.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Reviewer follow-up: valid product bug with solid evidence. Keep open as a real follow-up; should be prioritized ahead of cosmetic bootstrap polish.

title: aimgr bootstrap warns about missing git author identity in isolated launcher env
description:
## Discovered in
Manual Phase 1 bootstrap validation for `opencode-coder-bwrr` using the isolated `empty-project` launcher environment on 2026-04-18.

## Expected
Fresh isolated bootstrap should either avoid git-identity-dependent commit steps or present a clean success path without confusing author-identity warnings.

## Actual
`aimgr repo add` / `aimgr repo apply-manifest` / `aimgr repo sync` succeeded, but also emitted warnings that git author identity was unknown (for example `fatal: unable to auto-detect email address`).

## Repro
1. Create a fresh isolated launcher workspace with `bun run test:manual -- --mode=shell --fixture=empty-project`.
2. In that preserved environment, run either the public apply-manifest flow or a local-source fallback (`aimgr repo add` or `aimgr repo apply-manifest`, then `aimgr repo sync`).
3. Observe the output.

## Impact
This is non-blocking, but it adds confusing noise to the first-run bootstrap path and may make users think setup failed even when it succeeded.

## Evidence
- Manual launcher artifacts: `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder/.manual-test-runs/run-PnUQEF`, `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder/.manual-test-runs/run-YjR1ts`, `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder/.manual-test-runs/run-FHVtcp`

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Review verdict: VALID but correctly scoped at P3. What: git author identity warnings in isolated test environments are real and will appear for any user running bootstrap in a container or fresh env without git config. The bug description is accurate and the repro is concrete. Why it matters: it's cosmetic noise, not a blocker, but it degrades the first-run experience. Suggested action: keep as-is at P3. Defer — this is polish work, not install/setup-critical. Fix direction: either suppress git commit steps when identity is missing, or document that git config is a prerequisite.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Reviewer follow-up: valid but non-blocking polish issue. Keep open as deferred cleanup unless bootstrap UX polish is being handled immediately.
